verdict.instructions: In this Arabic Islamic lecture transcript, determine whether `matched_span_in_lecture` (surrounded by `context_before` and `context_after`) is an actual quotation/citation of `canonical_corpus_text` (`source_type`), or if it is merely ordinary speaker prose/explanation that happens to share words with the corpus text.

criteria.CORRECT: The speaker is genuinely quoting, reciting, or invoking this Quranic Ayah, Prophetic Hadith, or Dhikr (verbatim or as a direct religious citation in context).
criteria.FALSE: False positive: the words are ordinary conversational speech, fiqh explanation, or narrator/person names that coincidentally overlap with corpus vocabulary without quoting the text.
criteria.NOT_SURE: Ambiguous or partial paraphrase/meaning-only allusion where it is borderline whether the speaker intended a direct quotation.

boundary_status.instructions: Compare `immediate_transcript_before` against `unmatched_corpus_prefix_words`, and `immediate_transcript_after` against `unmatched_corpus_suffix_words`. Determine whether the speaker actually uttered additional words of this quote at the beginning or end (even with minor ASR spelling errors) that were accidentally cut off from `matched_span_in_lecture`. If the speaker intentionally stopped quoting and resumed normal commentary, select COMPLETE_SPAN.

criteria.COMPLETE_SPAN: The detected span captures all words of the quote that the speaker actually uttered in this segment (no words of the quote were cut off in the adjacent transcript).
criteria.MISSING_START: Words from `unmatched_corpus_prefix_words` appear inside `immediate_transcript_before` and were cut off from the beginning of the detection.
criteria.MISSING_END: Words from `unmatched_corpus_suffix_words` appear inside `immediate_transcript_after` and were cut off from the end of the detection.
criteria.MISSING_BOTH: Words of the quote were cut off from BOTH the beginning (`immediate_transcript_before`) and the end (`immediate_transcript_after`).

merge_suggestion.instructions: `neighbor_findings` lists the engine findings immediately before (`previous`) and/or after (`next`) this one, with the transcript words between them (`gap_transcript_text`). The engine often splits ONE quotation into separate findings when an ASR typo, a garbled or missing word, or a short repetition breaks the match; a neighbour may even be linked to a different reference. Decide, independently of `verdict`, whether this finding and a neighbour are consecutive parts of the same quoted text (compare the spans and the corpus texts) and should be one finding. Do not merge two different texts quoted one after the other.

criteria.NO_MERGE: This finding is a separate quotation (or the neighbour is a different text, or the gap is unrelated speech).
criteria.MERGE_WITH_PREVIOUS: This finding and the `previous` neighbour are parts of the same quotation.

merge_gap_type.instructions: Only meaningful when you suggest a merge: what are the words in `gap_transcript_text` between the parts?

criteria.PART_OF_QUOTE: The gap is empty, or it is mis-transcribed / garbled / repeated words of the quoted text itself.
criteria.COMMENTARY: The gap is the speaker's own interjection or explanation between two parts of the same quotation.
